description: 4 exemplars (1 de) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Exemplars are the four When-to-use cases: choosing an MCP tool, chaining tools across servers, troubleshooting an MCP tool error, and referencing MCP tools from a skill. Near-misses share the MCP vocabulary and route elsewhere: building a server (mcp-builder), a Sentry investigation that merely runs over MCP tools (sentry-integration, which this skill's Sentry section points to), and vetting a new server before connecting it (supply-chain-intake). Counterexamples guard the 'protocol' / 'server' vocabulary in unrelated work.

queries.q: which MCP tool should I use to look up the latest docs for this library?
chain the Jira and GitHub MCP servers: read the ticket, then find the PR that references it
the MCP tool call keeps returning a permission error — what am I doing wrong?
welche MCP-Tools soll der neue Command referenzieren, und in welcher Reihenfolge ruft er sie auf?
build an MCP server in TypeScript that exposes our internal search API as tools
queries.note: authoring a server rather than using existing ones → mcp-builder

queries.q: here's a Sentry issue URL — find out why it started failing after yesterday's deploy
queries.note: runs over Sentry MCP tools, but the ask is the error investigation → sentry-integration, which this skill's Sentry section points to

queries.q: is this third-party MCP server safe to connect before we add it to the config?
queries.note: intake vetting of a new server and its tool grants, not using a configured one → supply-chain-intake

queries.q: explain how the TCP three-way handshake works
queries.note: protocol vocabulary with no MCP involvement

queries.q: restart the staging web server after the config change
